summary: Prepare Core-owned sanlock repository and VM lease paths behind an unverified-hardware gate

guide.reason: The guide explicitly states that storage-lease automatic takeover is not available while hardware reset verification and Core acceptance are open.

api.reason: Additive Core membership and peer fields carry stable sanlock host IDs, exact NFS lease repository records and typed storage exclusion evidence. The native reset-verification gate remains false, so Controller does not offer storage-lease takeover; older Core omits the optional fields.

roadmap.reason: Storage lease remains unaccepted and the two-host plan retains partial status.

state.reason: The master owns stable sanlock host IDs and a monotonic allocator, exact repository lockspaces and a preparation generation. Native leases live on shared NFS; Controller stores no pool lease state.
state.record: Core pool-peer.json PoolMembership member SanlockHostID/allocator and StorageLease configuration on the master, replicated in signed pool authority records; a fresh Controller recovers the same record from the master's authenticated membership inventory.

verification.method: Before the workstation safety hold, a disposable Debian 13 native lab exercised per-repository libvirt leases and typed sanlock status reads; its limits are recorded in QA. After the hold, only static review, compile-only Go checks, API schema tests and repository privacy checks ran. The reset-verification status intentionally remains false, so no Core lockspace, authority holder, VM lease or promotion path has been activated end to end; physical watchdog and NFS timing evidence remain open.
